name: Dark Coral
lede: Dark Coral is a muted, brick-toned red, ColorHub's library name for a darkened shade of [[coral]], filed by the ISCC-NBS dictionary in 1955.

sections.title: A darkened coral
sections.body:
The name follows ColorHub's modifier grammar: "dark" plus the parent color [[coral]], the pink-red named for the marine animal and its skeleton [1]. The library records the swatch from the ISCC-NBS Dictionary of Color Names of 1955, in its block for strong red, and again from the xkcd color survey of 2010 [1]. No book in the ColorHub concordance treats "Dark Coral" as its own entry; the darkening is ColorHub's own description of where this shade sits relative to coral, not a historical name in its own right [1].

The nearest named neighbors on file are [[pastel-red]] and [[indian-red]], both close enough in hue and depth to be mistaken for it at a glance, with [[cedar-chest]] a shade duller [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a color near this swatch in 88 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.37 per cent, as photographed [2]. It plays a mid-tone role in most of its appearances and peaks in paintings from the 1890s [2]. It is disproportionately common in Kalighat and Rajput paintings from India in our sample, and in the work of Henri Matisse [2]. These are computed color matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
